images.title: Steps of the smallest angle
images.purpose: Show that angles of symmetry for a smallest angle of 90 degrees are 90, 180, 270 and 360, and 100 degrees cannot fit.
images.composition: One long horizontal line across the middle with wide space above and below.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal number line from 0 to 360 degrees in grey #6B7280, drawn to scale. Teal #0072B2 dots at 90, 180, 270 and 360, joined by 4 equal arcs above the line, each arc 90 degrees. One amber #E69F00 hollow circle at 100 degrees with a cross through it. Exactly 4 teal dots, 4 arcs, 1 crossed circle.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
tick spacing that is not to scale
images.takeaway: Every angle of symmetry is a step of the smallest angle.
images.description: A number line of turns with teal dots at 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees, and a crossed amber circle at 100 degrees.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say each step of 90 and explain why 100 would give a smaller fitting angle of 10.

image_decisions.why: The steps of the smallest angle are a picture idea; one number line carries it.
